what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, eleven commits, nine substantive, and the top of the last record was answered properly: the value arm no longer reports a ceiling as a decision. A coarse grid that could only ever return one of its own sixteen numbers now brackets, and a refinement decides -- 107 accounts sitting on exactly GBP 130 became a concentration of 1.9%, with interior optima on 257 of 263 and only one account still at the top of its grid. That is the difference between a per-customer decision and a rule wearing one, and it is the single most thesis-relevant thing this project has built. LANE 0 landed too, so this record is reachable by a draw, and publishing is live again -- the cause was never the deadline but two files git had never seen, and the receipt redesign the last record ordered was correctly REJECTED on analysis rather than built, because only the second gate can see what the commit is landing. Both of those items therefore leave focus. What the improved arm bought is a much sharper problem, and it is the world's, not the company's. Freed to choose, the arm chose a median of GBP 115/MWh and a +53% median bill -- roughly GBP 900 a year on a typical account -- and it is right to, because `simulation/market_switching_propensity.py:55` caps the world's annual switching rate at 22% once savings available pass GBP 400, and both sides cap the leave probability at 0.95. So the world models one in five leaving whether a rival is GBP 400 or GBP 2,000 cheaper, and one in twenty staying whatever they are charged. The arm has priced its entire book into the flat top of that curve, which is beyond anything the DESNZ series it was fitted to ever observed. This is the coupled-triad rule biting exactly where it was meant to: no company capability is complete until it has faced a world that can defeat it, and this world cannot defeat a supplier that gouges. It also weakens the headline comparison -- a +2.0pp belief-versus-truth gap between an estimator and a truth fitted from the same published series, read where neither has data, is co-calibration and not demonstrated inference. So the honest position is that the per-customer machinery is now real and the instrument that would judge it is not. On the previous focus: the brief again reports none of it drawn, and again the brief is wrong -- it counts maturity-map atom draws only, and three of the five items were non-atom instructions, two of which landed. The steer is working and unmeasured; that is now the third record in a row where this seat's own instrument would have told the next seat to give up on steers that were succeeding. The genuine drift is different and it repeated within this stretch: the arm rebuild -- 207 lines, and the best work here -- is sitting UNCOMMITTED in a shared tree with 462 untracked paths, which is the exact defect the last record caught on LANE 0 and fixed.

focus.what: Make the world's switching curve say when it is being read outside its own data. `_savings_to_rate` in `simulation/market_switching_propensity.py` is fitted to the DESNZ 2015-2025 series and returns a flat `_MAX_RATE = 0.22` for every savings figure above GBP 400, and `WORLD_MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY` caps the leave probability at 0.95. Do NOT invent a steeper elasticity. Make the out-of-calibration region explicit and reported at the seam -- the world's own equivalent of the `model_support_bound` the company arm already carries -- so that a run in which the company prices into the flat top is visible as unsupported extrapolation rather than a confident answer. Then re-run the arms comparison and record what the arm's choices look like once the world can say "I do not know".
focus.why: The thesis says the advantage must come from inference and there must be a baseline to beat. Neither claim can be made against a world that keeps 78% of a book whatever it charges, and the arm has put its whole book past GBP 400 of savings available where the curve is flat. R13 binds this: it is a baseline change, so it is made for fidelity to the data only and decided blind to what it does to the company's numbers -- an extrapolation flag is defensible because the series genuinely has no observations there, and a new number would not be. Done when a reader of the run can see which decisions were taken in a region the world has no evidence for, and the arm's verdict says so in its own words.

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
